scope: Theorem 5.2 (Planar exterior count) of the manuscript “Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders” (preprints/Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Quartic-Torus-Packets-for-Arbitrary-Orders-October-5-2026/quartic-torus-packets.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 015 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95c2a937da74097a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute τ > 0 with the following property. Fix m ∈ Z \ {0} and a bounded set Ω ⊂ Hm. For every primitive totally real quartic field K, every order O ⊂ K, every ordering of its real embeddings, and every chosen system of fractional R-ideal representatives for the ordinary classes, let M be defined by Equation (5.8). For all sufficiently large X, every rectangle R ⊂ Ω whose two side lengths are at least X−τ satisfies X z∈F, Tr z=m z∈R M(z) ≪m,Ω κ √ D area(R). (5.10) The implied constant and the threshold for X are uniform in the field, the order, the embedding ordering, the ideal representative system, the position of the rectangle, and its side lengths and aspect ratio.
